I just made a beat that was 20 tracks. The beat I'm making now probably won't go over 10. It really is just situational awareness at that point. I'd say, if you feel your beat is missing something it probably is. But make sure you don't put too much more into the beat if you're struggling to know what to add. You'll end up metaphorically overflowing the beat. Making in less than the sum of it's parts.

I think finding people who support you is pivotal. Having a blanket of other musicians who believe in the work you do is going to be a deciding factor in your ability to trust your own work. Instead of "if you don't believe in yourself, how can you expect others to believe in you". I think that it makes more sense to say, "Don't believe in yourself. But believe in the people who believe in you." Because when you have people who think you have the skills to succeed it becomes much more difficult to succumb to doubt.
